# Ironbark Sense — this week's outreach

## 1. Mary Major, VP Operations, Harborline Distribution

**Day 0 — Subject: Your Stackwise question from the webinar (answered, late)**

Hi Mary,

In our webinar Q&A three weeks ago you asked whether Ironbark Sense works with Stackwise. You should have had an answer that day. I'm sorry you didn't.

The straight answer: yes, but it's in beta. The integration is API-based and about three customers are running it live today. It isn't generally available yet, and I'd rather you hear that from me now than discover it mid-rollout.

I also saw the news about the fourth DC in Reno and 200 hires by summer. A new site with a new workforce is where pedestrian-proximity alerts and operator check-in tend to earn their keep fastest, because there are no habits to unlearn.

Would a 20-minute walkthrough of the Stackwise beta — what works, what's still rough — be useful? I can also send the Coldbrook Foods case study first if you'd prefer to read before talking.

Best,
[Name]

**Day 3 — Subject: What 38 forklifts at Coldbrook Foods showed over six months**

Hi Mary,

Following up with the data I mentioned, rather than a nudge.

Coldbrook Foods ran Ironbark Sense at one DC with 38 forklifts. Over six months, recorded near-miss events fell 60%. Forklift impacts went from 9 to 4 in the first 12 months. That's one site, so read it as a strong signal rather than a guarantee — but it's the kind of number that's hard to get any other way, because near-misses rarely get written up.

For Harborline, the interesting version is Reno: 200 new staff, a baseline from day one, and supervisors seeing impacts the same shift instead of after a damage report.

A pilot is 30 days, up to 10 trucks at one site, no charge. One option: run it at an existing DC now, so you have a comparison before Reno opens. Worth 20 minutes?

Best,
[Name]

**Day 8 — Subject: Pricing, the beta caveat, and an easy no**

Hi Mary,

Last note from me for now, with the two things people usually want before agreeing to a call.

Pricing starts at $45 per vehicle per month. Across roughly 120 trucks, that's a known figure you can put next to your current impact, damage and downtime costs.

The Stackwise caveat again: it's beta, about three customers live. If that's a blocker until it's generally available, tell me and I'll come back when it is — no sequence, no chasing.

If it isn't, the most useful next step is either a Stackwise walkthrough with someone from our integrations team, or a 30-day no-charge pilot on up to 10 trucks at one site. Which fits better — or neither?

Either way, good luck with the Reno build-out.

Best,
[Name]

## 2. John Stiles, Director of Safety, Northvale Cold Storage

**Subject: 12 new second-shift operators in Fresno**

Hi John,

Northvale Cold Storage's careers page leads with "safety-first culture" and is hiring 12 forklift operators for second shift. In my experience, onboarding a group of new operators onto a later shift is exactly when a safety director wants more visibility, not less.

Ironbark Sense is forklift telematics with pedestrian-proximity alerts, impact detection and operator check-in. At one DC with 38 trucks, Coldbrook Foods saw recorded near-miss events fall 60% over six months.

We offer a 30-day pilot on up to 10 trucks at one site, at no charge. Second shift at one of your two DCs would be a natural place to run it — you'd have a baseline before the new hires are fully up to speed.

Would 15 minutes next week be useful?

Best,
[Name]

## 3. Plan for Richard Roe, EHS Manager, Pellucid Beverages

**What I won't do**

- **No email of any kind.** He unsubscribed on 11 Feb 2026. That includes "just this one," calendar invites, sequences, or a colleague emailing on my behalf. Treat the opt-out as covering all email until he explicitly says otherwise.
- **No leading with the OSHA citation.** He knows. Opening with it reads as ambulance-chasing and, if there's litigation or an abatement process underway, he can't discuss it anyway. I also won't imply Ironbark Sense "would have prevented it" — I don't know the facts of the incident.
- **No LinkedIn pile-on** as a workaround while he's dealing with a citation.

**What I will do**

- **One phone call** (phone is OK per CRM), ideally mid-morning, not Monday. Script: I'm aware it's probably a heavy few weeks for EHS at Pellucid; I'm not calling about that. I sell forklift telematics, and if having another option on his radar is useful, I can send the Coldbrook case study — *only if he gives me permission to email*, which I'll note in the CRM with date and time before sending anything. If it's not useful, I'll thank him and go away.
- **One voicemail maximum** if he doesn't pick up, then stop. Log the outcome either way.
- If he says no or asks not to be called, mark Do Not Call and close the record.

**Why:** the unsubscribe is both a legal line and a trust signal. The citation makes him a plausible buyer eventually, but only if we're the vendor that behaved well while he was under pressure.

## 4. Note to marketing

Re: "Ironbark cuts forklift accidents by 60%. Guaranteed."

Please don't use this. The 60% figure is *recorded near-miss events* at one Coldbrook DC (38 trucks) over six months — not accidents. Impacts fell 9 to 4 (56%), also one site, small numbers. "Guaranteed" is a claim we can't support and creates legal exposure, especially with prospects already facing OSHA scrutiny. Recorded near-misses also often *rise* at first once you start measuring, so the headline could backfire in a pilot.

Suggested alternative: "One DC cut recorded forklift near-misses 60% in six months. Here's how." Specific, sourced, defensible.

## 5. Rationale

**Mary Major:** She asked a direct question and got silence, so email one owns that and answers honestly — including that Stackwise is beta with ~3 customers live. Overselling the integration to a 120-truck prospect is how you lose the account later. Reno and the 200 hires give a legitimate timing hook. Each follow-up adds something concrete (case-study data, pricing) and the last one offers a clean exit. CTA: beta walkthrough or pilot, her choice.

**John Stiles:** Cold outreach, so I used what's actually true of *his* company — the careers page and second-shift hiring — and deliberately ignored the Northvale Logistics fine, which is a different company in a different state and would be both wrong and embarrassing. CTA: 15 minutes, with the pilot as the obvious next step.

**Richard Roe:** Compliance first, decency second, pipeline third. A single respectful call preserves the relationship for when he's ready.
